answer: Reputation-decayed entry pricing. Each new identity starts on a ledge of low trust and pays an entry fee that doubles with every sibling identity sharing the same funding source or device fingerprint. Costs decay only after sustained honest activity, so a fresh swarm pays exponentially while a lone newcomer pays little. Attackers must spread real capital across many independent roots to avoid the multiplier, raising the per-identity cost far above reward. Honest users form a haven of cheap entry; sybils face a nebula of compounding fees.
